title: removeCollateralWLpTo/decollateralizeWLp and liquidateWLp never verify the (wLp, tokenId) pair belongs to the position on partial or zero removal
description: Discovery: MODIFIER-01 / Module L sibling diff (confirms and deepens DP1-1). harvestTo() and getCollWLpAmt() both require __posCollInfos[_posId].ids[_wlp].contains(_tokenId), but removeCollateralWLpTo() only performs the membership check (ids.remove) inside the newWLpAmt == 0 branch. For _amt < balanceOfLp(_tokenId) (including _amt == 0) the function harvests and unwraps NFT _tokenId, which PosManager owns for every collateralized wLp, on behalf of whichever _posId the caller controls. Second entry point: liquidateWLp lets the liquidator pass any _tokenId; getCollWLpAmt returns 0 for a non-member token, so wLpAmtToBurn = 0 and removeCollateralWLpTo(_posId, wLp, victimToken, 0, ...) still runs _harvest and credits the foreign NFT's pending rewards to the liquidated position's pendingRewards.
root_cause: Authorization is per positionId (onlyAuthorized(_posId)) but the asset acted on is identified by a caller-supplied (wLp, tokenId) whose membership in that position is enforced only on the emptying path; PosManager, as global NFT owner, passes the wLp's onlyOwner checks for any tokenId.

harm.who: owners of positions that collateralized a wLp NFT
harm.loses_what: all but 1 unit of the LP behind the NFT plus accrued rewards
harm.magnitude: balanceOfLp(tokenId) - 1 per victim NFT; victim position is then undercollateralized and liquidatable

exploit_trace: 1. Victim collateralizes wLp NFT N (balanceOfLp = 1000) in position V; PosManager owns N.
2. Attacker owns an unrelated position A and calls InitCore.decollateralizeWLp(A, wLp, N, 999, attacker): onlyAuthorized(A), whitelist and mode checks pass.

3. PosManager.removeCollateralWLpTo(A, wLp, N, 999, attacker): newWLpAmt = 1, membership check skipped; _harvest credits N's rewards to pendingRewards[A]; wLp.unwrap(N, 999, attacker) executes as PosManager (owner).
4. ensurePositionHealth(A) checks only A, unchanged, so the call succeeds; attacker claims rewards via claimPendingRewards(A, ...) and V is now near-zero collateral (liquidatable).
5. Reward-only variant: _amt = 0, or a self-liquidation of A through liquidateWLp with victim tokenId.

preconditions.text: a whitelisted wLp NFT is collateralized in another position

postconditions.text: victim position collateral value collapses while its NFT stays registered

title: Repay pause (pool or mode canRepay=false) also disables liquidation because liquidate() routes through _repay
description: Discovery: MISSING-02 (restriction coverage). _liquidateInternal calls _repay, which requires getPoolConfig(pool).canRepay && getModeStatus(mode).canRepay. A guardian pausing repay (to stop borrower repayments during an incident or oracle problem) therefore also blocks every liquidate/liquidateWLp on that pool/mode, while interest keeps accruing and collateral prices move. Unlike borrow/withdraw pauses, there is no separate liquidation switch and no bypass for liquidation.
root_cause: Liquidation reuses the user-facing repay path including its pause flags instead of an internal repay without status checks.

harm.loses_what: collateral coverage; bad debt accrues because underwater positions cannot be liquidated during the pause
harm.magnitude: unbounded by pause duration and price move

exploit_trace: 1. Guardian sets canRepay=false on pool P (or mode M) via Config.setPoolConfig/setModeStatus.
2. Collateral price falls; position X in M becomes health < 1e18.
3. Liquidator calls liquidate(X, P, shares, poolOut, min): _repay reverts with REPAY_PAUSED.
4. Borrower cannot repay either; debt grows with interest until unpause, by which time the position may be underwater (bad debt socialized to lenders).

preconditions.text: guardian pauses repay on a pool or mode with live borrows

title: MoneyMarketHook sweeps its entire WNATIVE/ETH balance to any caller with returnNative, and repay over-pull plus per-param msg.value wrapping can source those stray funds
description: Discovery: AC-03 (periphery contract access control). The hook is a shared custodian but treats its balance as the caller's. (a) With returnNative = true, execute withdraws the hook's whole WNATIVE balance and forwards the whole ETH balance to msg.sender. (b) _handleRepay pulls debtShareToAmtCurrent(_params.shares) from the user, but core.repay only repays min(shares, position debt shares), so a WNATIVE repay with shares above the debt leaves the excess in the hook (and for non-WNATIVE tokens it is stuck). (c) _handleDeposit calls WNATIVE.deposit{value: msg.value}() once per WNATIVE deposit param, so with two params the second wrap is paid from stray hook ETH. ETH sent with execute but not consumed by a WNATIVE deposit also stays.
root_cause: The hook holds no per-user accounting for transient funds and permissionlessly releases whatever balance it holds to the next caller.

harm.who: users who over-repay with WNATIVE or send surplus msg.value
harm.magnitude: the surplus left in the hook per user; any later caller takes it

exploit_trace: 1. Victim calls execute with a WNATIVE repay of shares larger than the position's debt shares; the hook pulls W tokens, core repays only the debt, the excess E stays in the hook as WNATIVE.
2. Attacker calls execute with an empty OperationParams for a fresh position and returnNative = true.
3. The hook unwraps its full WNATIVE balance and sends all ETH (including E) to the attacker.

preconditions.text: surplus WNATIVE/ETH remains in the hook after a prior call

title: Config has no way to remove a pool from a mode's borrow set (borrow factor must stay >= 1e18) so a single pool cannot be disabled for a mode
description: Discovery: MISSING-01 (missing unsetters). setBorrFactors_e18 only adds to borrTokens and requires factor >= 1e18, and no function removes entries from borrTokens/collTokens. Collateral can be neutralized with factor 0, but borrowing a given pool in a given mode can only be stopped by pausing the pool for all modes (PoolConfig.canBorrow) or the mode for all pools (ModeStatus.canBorrow). A mis-listed borrow pool stays borrowable by that mode.
root_cause: Add-only EnumerableSet configuration with a lower-bounded factor and no remover.
exploit_trace: 1. Governor lists a pool P in mode M by mistake or P later turns risky.
2. Governor cannot remove P from M and cannot set a disabling factor; only a global pause of P or M is possible.
3. Users in M keep borrowing P until the broader pause.

preconditions.text: a pool must be disabled for one mode only
